case: Netflix DVD-to-streaming pivot and Qwikster reversal (2007-2011)

claude.performance_metric: split reversed ~23 days after announcement; ~1 million subscribers lost; >50% share-price decline (July–Oct 2011)
claude.rationale: This is an intra-firm pivot with no ownership-boundary crossing (§1, §7); the planned split of product (T4) and processes/websites (T5) was cancelled before launch ("no Qwikster," §2), so neither crossed any boundary — gap_45=0 and gap_56=0 (T6 people stayed within one firm and never separated, §2/§4-P5). The product/process disruption was only a hypothetical of the abandoned plan, and §4-P5 explicitly states "No ownership-crossing fracture; the reorganization stayed within one firm and was undone before launch," so p4_pathway=0 and p5_pathway=0 at the documented outcome. Separately, §4 documents leadership strategic-intent error (Hastings' acknowledgment of poor communication) → t1_archetype=1, and customer rejection of the unbundled two-service value logic → t2_model=1.

gemini.performance_metric: >50% share-price decline and ~1 million subscriber loss
gemini.rationale: The dossier explicitly notes no ownership boundary was crossed, meaning no structural gaps at closing occurred (gap_45=0, gap_56=0). However, the attempted internal split caused documented product-process disruption (p4_pathway=1) due to customer confusion over managing two separate websites, leading to the reversal of the plan.

grok.performance_metric: split reversed ~23 days after announcement; ~1M subscribers lost, shares lost >50% value
grok.rationale: Dossier section 2 shows no ownership boundary crossed and T3 null (no Qwikster entity launched). Section 4 documents P4 product-process disruption via the two-website plan that caused customer confusion and reversal. P5 is absent (no ownership-crossing fracture). T1 and T2 non-cascade channels are both documented as leadership/model errors.
